event_name: Honors Scholarship Saxophone Quartet – Chamber Music Connection
event_description: The Hochstein Honor’s Scholarship Saxophone Quartet is comprised of four outstanding high school students from the Greater Rochester area who perform regularly in the community and for Hochstein functions. The quartet features a wide range of saxophones, including the soprano, alto, tenor and baritone saxophones and is at home playing in diverse musical styles ranging from classical and jazz to contemporary popular music. Soprano saxophonist Corrina Penner is graduating from Churchville-Chili High School and will be studying psychology at Roberts Wesleyan University in the fall. Alto saxophonist Drew Daniels currently attends Churchville-Chili High School and also specializes on the oboe. Tenor saxophonist Reegan Fenn is graduating from Marion Senior High School and will be attending the Arkansas Horseshoeing School to become a farrier; and baritone saxophonist, Maxwell Bolzner, who also specializes on the electric bass, is graduating from Webster High School and will be studying Chemical Engineering at MCC next year. The director, Nancy Boone-Bahr, has been teaching saxophone and clarinet at The Hochstein School since 1993 and is thrilled to be working with such incredible individuals.

event_description: Tyler Westcott is a poet, singer/songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist based out of Buffalo, NY. Westcott breathes new life into roots music spanning multiple genres and decades. Also creating new music inspired by the old. He specializes in storytelling, songwriting, folk, country blues, traditional jazz, bluegrass and old time, western swing, and more. Armed with his trusty guitar, banjo, and harmonica, & the gift of the gab, he has a knack for describing the human condition with humor and joy, Often in timely and topical songs reflecting the current state of the world. Westcott will guide you through a myriad of genres and decades of eclectic roots music while seamlessly weaving in his own original cuts. event_name: Alan Harris 90th Birthday Celebration Concert
event_description: Please join us in celebrating the 90th birthday and remarkable legacy of Alan Harris—beloved teacher, mentor, cellist, and friend—at a special concert and reception honoring a lifetime of music-making and teaching. This gathering brings together friends, family, and former cello students to recognize Professor Harris’s profound impact on generations of musicians and the musical life of our community. The celebration will feature a concert of cello solo and ensemble music, performed by former students and colleagues, followed by a reception where we can reconnect, share stories, and raise a glass to Alan’s extraordinary career and enduring influence. Whether you studied with Alan, performed alongside him, or were inspired by his teaching and generosity of spirit, we hope you’ll be part of this joyful tribute. Let’s come together to celebrate 90 years of Alan Harris—and a legacy that continues to resonate through music and community.

event_name: Hochstein All-School Rally
event_description: Families and students of The Hochstein School, you won't want to miss our very first All-School Rally on Thursday, September 10 from 6pm-7pm in the Performance Hall! Whether you're just joining our Hochstein community or you've been attending classes for years, you'll have a blast at this free family event. There will be live music and dance performances, skits by your favorite Hochstein staff and faculty, Hochstein swag and giveaways, and snacks to enjoy. All ages welcome FREE but registration is encouraged

event_name: ESL Rochester Fringe Festival: Miles Davis Animated
event_description: Miles Davis Animated brings the music of Miles Davis’ groundbreaking 1950s–60s era to life with a creative twist: animated visuals, expressive tap dance, and a powerhouse ensemble of performers. Audiences will be visually transported by larger-than-life cartoon illustrations from Dave Chisholm’s acclaimed graphic novel Miles Davis and the Search for the Sound. These evocative visuals, paired with bold musical improvisation and kinetic tap rhythms, create a multi-sensory experience that honors Miles’ artistry while reinventing it for new generations. Classic works from Miles Davis’ legendary catalog are interpreted by a stellar ensemble including trumpeter and cartoonist Dave Chisholm, pianist Greg Woodsbie, saxophonist Colin Gordon, bassist David Arenius, and drummer Aaron Staebell. Tap dancers Cheryl Johnson and Laurie Coles will animate the music with percussive rhythm and emotional nuance, transforming the stage into a living, breathing soundscape.

event_name: Live from Hochstein: Rochester Philharmonic Orchestra
event_description: The Hochstein School's Live from Hochstein concert series returns this fall with a new lineup of free noontime performances beginning Wednesday, October 14, 2026, and continuing weekly through December 16, 2026. Concerts take place from 12:10–12:50 p.m. in the Hochstein Performance Hall and are open to the public at no charge. These concerts are presented in partnership with WXXI and broadcast live on WXXI Classical 91.5 and rebroadcast at 10 p.m. the day of the concert. The Rochester Philharmonic Orchestra kicks off our fall Live from Hochstein season with Jake Taniguichi conducting. Full program details to be announced soon. All ages welcome FREE Preregistration is encouraged Hochstein welcomes community and school groups to attend Live From Hochstein. So we can better serve the needs of your group, please call our Front Office at (585) 454-4596 with the estimated number of guests and buses we can expect. About the Rochester Philharmonic Orchestra The Rochester Philharmonic Orchestra (RPO) has been committed to enriching and inspiring our community through the art of music since its inception in 1922. The RPO presents approximately 150 concerts and broadcasts per year, serving up to 170,000 people through ticketed events, education and community engagement activities, and concerts in schools and community centers throughout the region. Andreas Delfs was named music director in 2021. Principal Pops Conductor Jeff Tyzik, now in his 30th season, has earned a national reputation for excellence in pops programming during his tenure with the RPO. The RPO reaches over 15,000 youths through its education programs. About Jake Taniguichi Jake Taniguchi is the Assistant Conductor of the RPO and Music Director of the RPYO. In the 2026–27 season, he will lead numerous programs with both ensembles, including community, family, and education concerts, and will take the RPYO on an international tour to Vienna, Salzburg, and Prague. Taniguchi has served on the conducting faculty at the Cleveland Institute of Music, as principal conductor of the Hawaiʻi Chamber Music Festival (HCMF), and as assistant and cover conductor for the Hawaiʻi Symphony Orchestra, Omaha Symphony, Grant Park Music Festival Orchestra, and the Indiana University Ballet and Opera Theater. He has collaborated with distinguished conductors including Leonard Slatkin, Dane Lam, Mei-Ann Chen, Jeffery Kahane, and Anthony Parnther, as well as soloists including violinists Jaime Laredo, Jessica Lee, and Stefan Jackiw; pianists Michelle Cann, Joyce Yang, Adam Golka, and David Kaplan; and mezzo-soprano Michelle DeYoung. A fervent advocate for new music, he has fostered artistic partnerships with composers Marcos Balter, Sebastian Currier, Billy Childs, Keith Fitch, Christopher Cerrone, and Joan Tower, among others. Devoted to nurturing a lifelong enthusiasm for music, Taniguchi has worked with numerous schools, youth organizations, and educational programs, including the Masaki School of Music, Kamehameha Schools, Mid-Pacific Institute School of the Arts, Oshkosh Youth Symphony Orchestra, and HCMF's Young Artist Program. Taniguchi holds degrees from the Indiana University Jacobs School of Music, Northwestern University Bienen School of Music, and the Cleveland Institute of Music. His conducting mentors include JoAnn Falletta, Victor Yampolsky, Thomas Wilkins, Jeffery Meyer, and Arthur Fagen.

event_name: Live from Hochstein: Huiping Cai, piano
event_description: The Hochstein School's Live from Hochstein concert series returns this fall with a new lineup of free noontime performances beginning Wednesday, October 14, 2026, and continuing weekly through December 16, 2026. Concerts take place from 12:10–12:50 p.m. in the Hochstein Performance Hall and are open to the public at no charge. These concerts are presented in partnership with WXXI and broadcast live on WXXI Classical 91.5 and rebroadcast at 10 p.m. the day of the concert. Hochstein faculty member Huiping Cai, piano, presents "Liszt at 140," a program that will explore the many faces of love in Liszt’s music, from the poetic devotion of Petrarch’s Sonetto 104 del Petrarca, to the dramatic entanglements of Verdi’s Rigoletto, and culminating in the heroic passion and struggle of the Ballade No. 2 in B Minor. All ages welcome FREE Preregistration is encouraged Hochstein welcomes community and school groups to attend Live From Hochstein. So we can better serve the needs of your group, please call our Front Office at (585) 454-4596 with the estimated number of guests and buses we can expect. About Huiping Cai An engaging pianist with “dignified and mature approach” (Third Coast Review), Huiping Cai is renowned for her lyricism, musicality, and formidable technique. She has won numerous awards in competitions, including the First Prize and Audience Award at the 2023 New York Franz Liszt International Piano Competition. She also received first prizes at the 2022 Los Angeles International Liszt Competition; the 2019 Chopin International Piano Competition in Hartford, Connecticut; the 2018 Miami Music Festival Piano Concerto Competition; and the 2017 Philadelphia International Piano Competition. Huiping made her Carnegie Hall debut at the Weill Recital Hall and Stern Auditorium Perelman Stage with the Orchestra of St. Luke’s in 2023. She has performed piano concertos with the Evergreen Symphony Orchestra, Hong Kong VTC Symphony Orchestra, Jalisco Philharmonic Orchestra, Kazakhstan National Symphony Orchestra, Miami Music Festival Orchestra, Orchestra of St. Luke’s, Shenzhen Symphony Orchestra, and Temple University Symphony Orchestra. Huiping has also been a featured piano soloist on Philadelphia’s WRTI radio, Florida’s classical WSMR, and WFMT’s Dame Myra Hess Memorial Concerts in Chicago. Huiping is currently a candidate for the Doctor of Musical Arts in Piano Performance and Literature at the Eastman School of Music, serving as a Teaching Assistant for Alan Chow while also pursuing a Master of Music degree in Piano Accompanying & Chamber Music with Dr. Andrew Harley. She received her Bachelor of Music degree in Piano Performance and Music Theory from Temple University and her Master of Music from the New England Conservatory where she studied with Dang Thai Son and held a Teaching Assistantship.

event_description: The Hochstein School's Live from Hochstein concert series returns this fall with a new lineup of free noontime performances beginning Wednesday, October 14, 2026, and continuing weekly through December 16, 2026. Concerts take place from 12:10–12:50 p.m. in the Hochstein Performance Hall and are open to the public at no charge. Pegasus Rising, an offshoot of Rochester's Pegasus Early Music, is a competitive mentorship program that supports the next generation of professional early musicians. Based in New York City, Quartet Novalis seeks to bring a fresh perspective to the string quartet repertoire by uncovering old concepts of sound and musical understanding. By performing on historically-appropriate instruments, the group is able to draw out subtle and highly nuanced textures and impressions, while breathing life into repertoire that has fallen by the wayside. Concerts take place from 12:10–12:50 p.m. in the Hochstein Performance Hall and are open to the public at no charge. These concerts are presented in partnership with WXXI and broadcast live on WXXI Classical 91.5 and rebroadcast at 10 p.m. the day of the concert. John Dawson's Live from Hochstein performance, "French Perspectives in Percussion," highlights a selection of trends, styles, and approaches found in French composition of the last 50 years. The program features three guitar works by French composer Roland Dyens reimagined on the marimba. In each of these works, one will hear a blend of Dyens's French classical training with popular styles from Brazil. Also on the program is Philippe Manoury's Solo de vibraphone, from his monumental percussion work, Les Livres des Claviers, or Book of Keyboards. A staple in 20th century contemporary keyboard repertoire, the work offers a soloistic approach to music inspired by both spectral and serial traditions. French influence on percussion would be incomplete without a mention of French rudimental drumming: Pablo Rieppi's solos from Rhythmic Roots create a rudimental fusion between French, Brazilian, and American rhythmic influences. event_name: Live from Hochstein: Jiao Sun, piano
event_description: The Hochstein School's Live from Hochstein concert series returns this fall with a new lineup of free noontime performances beginning Wednesday, October 14, 2026, and continuing weekly through December 16, 2026. Concerts take place from 12:10–12:50 p.m. in the Hochstein Performance Hall and are open to the public at no charge. These concerts are presented in partnership with WXXI and broadcast live on WXXI Classical 91.5 and rebroadcast at 10 p.m. the day of the concert. From the intimate voices of the Baroque era to the vibrant colors and nuanced language of early twentieth-century music, virtuosic and expressive pianist Jiao Sun invites you on a profound and evocative musical journey. This concert unfolds as a gallery of vivid sound portraits—interweaving reflective, delicate melodies with moments of brilliance, virtuosity, and expressive depth. Through contrasting eras and musical landscapes, each work becomes a glimpse of light emerging through the stillness of winter. Whether you are tuning in during a midday lunch break in search of a moment of beauty and reflection, or you are a lifelong classical music enthusiast, this captivating program offers something to savor, discover, and remember. Join us for an enchanting solo piano celebration, and let the music illuminate your winter afternoon! All ages welcome FREE Preregistration is encouraged Hochstein welcomes community and school groups to attend Live From Hochstein. So we can better serve the needs of your group, please call our Front Office at (585) 454-4596 with the estimated number of guests and buses we can expect.
